Chapter 8: The Trouble with Hierarchies—When Respect Gets in the Way.
Now, respect is usually a wonderful thing. But what happens when showing respect actually becomes a barrier?
In a lot of cultures, there's this strong idea that you should know your place—defer to elders, follow the chain of command, and never rock the boat. On the surface, it sounds harmonious, right? But sometimes, these values can actually trip us up—especially when a team needs to move fast, or when honest feedback could save the day.
Picture a team racing against the clock on a high-stakes project. The leader’s got a plan, but one of the newer folks spots a flaw. They pause, second-guess themselves, and wonder, “Is it really my place to speak up?” The moment slips by... and that mistake? It goes unchecked. Later, when things unravel, everyone’s thinking—why didn’t anybody say something?
And this isn’t just about one team, or one company. You’ll find it in hospitals, on flight decks, even in classrooms. That urge to be respectful, to keep the peace, can sometimes keep people from sharing what really matters.
Sometimes the price is just a missed chance or a minor setback. But other times, it’s much more serious.
There’s a striking example from airline safety research. Investigators found that, in some crashes, the problem wasn’t with the plane or the equipment at all. It was that co-pilots or crew members felt too hesitant, too deferential, to challenge the captain’s authority. Out of respect, they held back—and disaster followed.
So what’s the real lesson here? The very values that keep a group close can also hold it back when it matters most.
But here’s the good news: there’s a way forward. The key is to build environments where everyone feels safe and encouraged to speak up. Where questions aren’t just tolerated—they’re welcomed. And where mistakes? They’re seen as moments to learn, not reasons to point fingers.
It’s not about tossing out tradition or ignoring the value of respect. It’s about finding that sweet spot—where everyone, no matter their role, feels empowered to contribute their best.
